newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool rises to 22-month high this week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool rises to 22-month high this week.

text.p: Limited supplies of wool at this week's Australian auctions in Sydney and Melbourne again saw prices maintain their upward trend, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said on Friday.
The Wool International eastern market indicator average ended the week at a 22-month high of 726 Australian cents (US$5.45) a kilogram clean, up 12 cents on the week, it said.
"Widespread competition, led by the Japanese trading houses for limited supplies, saw auction prices maintain their upward trend of recent weeks," the council said in its weekly market review.
Factors in the market essentially remain unchanged this week, the council said.

These comprised limited supply; restocking the pipeline; no clear signals as yet of increasing consumer demand in some major markets; increased though unexpected buying by China, helped by a weaker Australian dollar and widespread competition except for traders and mills in Continental Europe being relatively quiet.
A total of 48,950 bales were offered at the week's auctions, of which would-be sellers passed in 5.4 percent.
Pastoral house Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said market confidence has not abated and all indications are that the upward trend will continue.
Wool International, the official body charged with disposing of Australia's wool stockpile, said it sold 16,744 bales in the week ended June 12, reducing its stockpile to 1,606,674 bales.

In the Sydney Futures Exchange wool futures market a total of 254 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended Thursday and open interest increased by 64 contracts to close at 1,225.
The near August contract closed 18 cents up at 887 cents a kilogram clean.
Next week's sales will be in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with 77,000 bales rostered for sale.
